Export an obis_h3 store to hive-partitioned Parquet

Source: R/export.R
obis_h3_export_parquet.Rd

Writes the indicator layers of a store built by build_obis_h3_duckdb() to a directory of hive-partitioned Parquet files that a static web app can read directly with DuckDB-WASM (one small file per map layer and H3 resolution):

Usage

obis_h3_export_parquet(
  con,
  dir_out,
  release,
  res_decade = 1:5,
  parent_res = c(`6` = 2L, `7` = 3L),
  parent_res_taxon = c(`6` = 0L, `7` = 0L),
  parent_min_rows = 50000,
  max_open = EXPORT_MAX_OPEN,
  compression = "zstd",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  decades = seq(1960L, 2020L, by = 10L),
  esn = 50L,
  memory_limit = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

con

connection from obis_store_connect() (read-only is fine).

dir_out

output directory; files go under dir_out/release/.

release

release tag, e.g. "v20260728" (the OBIS snapshot date the store was built from); recorded in release.json.

res_decade

H3 resolutions for the decade layers (default 1-5).

parent_res

named integer vector, fine resolution -> parent resolution, for the all and eov layers: those resolutions are written one file per parent cell (res=<r>/p=<parent>/). Default c("6" = 2L, "7" = 3L); NULL writes every resolution whole.

parent_res_taxon

the same for the taxon layer (default c("6" = 0L, "7" = 0L), the base cell).

parent_min_rows

a (layer key, res) with at most this many rows is written whole even when its res is in parent_res (default 50000).

max_open

max partitions written by one COPY (default 100); each open partition holds a file open, so keep it under the process limit (ulimit -n, 256 on macOS by default).

compression

Parquet compression codec (default "zstd").

overwrite

replace an existing dir_out/release/ (default FALSE: stop).

decades

decades (first year) to export in the decade layers; default 1960-2020. NULL exports every decade present.

esn

expected sample size for ES(n) in the decade layers; default 50 (as in the store).

memory_limit

optional DuckDB memory_limit (e.g. "24GB").

threads

optional DuckDB thread count (e.g. 8).

verbose

print progress and the summary (default TRUE).

Value

invisibly, a character vector of the files written (absolute paths).

Details

<dir_out>/<release>/
  release.json                              build metadata, row counts, layout, columns, file manifest
  all/res=<1..5>/data_0.parquet             idx_h3 (all taxa, all years)
  all/res=<6,7>/p=<parent>/data_0.parquet   the fine res, one file per parent cell
  eov/eov=<eov>/res=<r>/data_0.parquet      idx_h3_eov
  taxon/rank=<rank>/taxon=<taxon>/res=<r>/  idx_h3_taxon (phylum / class / order)
  decade/all/decade=<yyy0>/res=<r>/         per decade, all taxa  (res in res_decade)
  decade/eov/eov=<eov>/decade=<yyy0>/res=<r>/  per decade and EOV (res in res_decade)
  stats.parquet                             value ranges per layer x key x res x variable
  taxon_groups.parquet                      the taxa and EOVs available, with totals and paths
  files.parquet                             manifest: layer, path, url_path, rows, bytes per file

Every indicator file has the columns h3 (lowercase hex string), cell_id, n, sp, shannon, simpson, es; the partition keys live in the path (read with hive_partitioning = true). The decade layers are computed from occ_h3 with the same SQL builder as idx_h3 / idx_h3_eov (so the math is identical to the store): n = records, sp = distinct species, Shannon, Simpson and ES(esn), grouped by cell and decade = floor(date_year / 10) * 10; records without a year are left out of the decade layers. EOV membership is the store's eov table (occ_h3.aphiaid = eov.taxonID), as in obis_eov_bake(). Layers whose source tables are missing (e.g. no idx_h3_eov in a store without taxonomy) are skipped with a message.

Partition values are percent-encoded by DuckDB (a space becomes %20), and DuckDB decodes them on read. A static web server decodes the URL once, so a browser must request the on-disk name with % itself encoded (%2520); taxon_groups.parquet carries both path (on disk) and url_path (to fetch), and files.parquet lists every file with both forms. Each partition is exactly one data_0.parquet.

Parent partitions for the fine resolutions. A whole res-7 layer is tens of MB, too much for a browser to load at once, so the resolutions named in parent_res are split by parent cell: every row of all/res=7/ goes to all/res=7/p=<h3 of its res-3 parent>/data_0.parquet (default res 6 by its res-2 parent, res 7 by its res-3 parent), and a viewer loads only the parent cells that cover its viewport. The taxon layer uses parent_res_taxon (default the res-0 base cell: res-3 parents would make over a million files across ~5k taxa). A (layer key, res) with at most parent_min_rows rows stays one whole file, since splitting it would only add requests. The decade layers are never split (their default resolutions are 1-5). files.parquet has a parent column (the partition's parent cell, NULL for a whole file; its resolution is the parent resolution), and each layer in release.json lists the parent_res actually used.

stats.parquet has one row per (layer, key, decade, res, variable) with min, p02, p50, p98, max and n_cells (cells with a non-NULL value; a variable NULL everywhere in a partition gets a row with NULL ranges and n_cells 0), for colour ramps. key is the EOV or taxon name (” for the all-taxa layers), rank the taxon rank (” otherwise), decade NA outside the decade layers.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- obis_store_connect("~/data/obis/obis_h3.duckdb")
obis_h3_export_parquet(con, "~/data/obis-h3", "v20260728")
} # }
